records.text: For thus says the Lord Almighty: Once more I will shake heaven and earth, the sea and the dry land.
His voice shook the earth then, but now He has promised, saying, “Yet once more I will shake not only the earth but also the heaven.”
Now “yet once more” indicates the removal of the things shaken, as things that have been made, so that the things not shaken may remain.
And I will shake all the nations, and the choice things of all the nations shall come; and I will fill this house with glory, says the Lord Almighty.
Then you will see and fear and be astonished in heart, for the wealth of sea, nations, and peoples will turn toward you. There will come to you
herds of camels, and camels from Madiam and Gaipha will cover you. They will all come from Saba, bringing gold and carrying frankincense, and they will proclaim the Lord’s salvation as good news.
All Kedar’s sheep will gather to you, and Nabaioth’s rams will come to you. They will be offered acceptably upon My altar, and My house of prayer will be glorified.
The silver is Mine and the gold is Mine, says the Lord Almighty.
Who am I, and who are my people, that we had strength to offer willingly unto Thee in this manner? All things are Thine, and of Thine own have we given unto Thee.
For we are resident strangers before Thee, and sojourners, as all our fathers were: our days upon earth are as a shadow, and there is no endurance.
Lord our God, all this abundance that I have prepared for a house to be built for Thy holy name is from Thy hand, and everything is Thine.

For the latter glory of this house will be greater than the former, says the Lord Almighty; in this place I will give peace, says the Lord Almighty, and peace of soul as a possession for everyone building to raise this sanctuary.”
The glory of the Lord entered the house by the way of the gate facing east.
A spirit lifted me and brought me into the inner court. Look—the house was full of the glory of the Lord.
Peace I leave with you; My peace I give you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your heart be troubled or afraid.
On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, in the second year under Darius, the word of the Lord came to Haggai the prophet, saying:
Please direct your hearts from this day onward; from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month and from the day the sanctuary of the Lord was founded, put it in your hearts:
“Thus says the Lord Almighty: Ask the priests about the law, saying:
to distinguish between the holy and the profane, and between the unclean and the clean.
And you shall instruct the sons of Israel in all the statutes which the Lord spoke unto them by the hand of Moses.
If someone takes holy meat in the edge of his garment and the edge of his garment touches bread, cooked food, wine, oil or any food, will it become holy?” The priests answered, “No.”

Speak unto Aaron and his sons, saying: This is the law of the sin offering. In the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offering, they shall slaughter the offerings for sin before the Lord; they are most holy.
The priest who offers it up shall eat it. It shall be eaten in a holy place, in the court of the Tent of Testimony.
Whosoever touches its flesh shall be sanctified; and if any of its blood is sprinkled upon a garment, what it was sprinkled upon shall be washed in a holy place.
Haggai said, “If one defiled through a dead person touches any of these, will it be defiled?” The priests answered, “It will be defiled.”
Whosoever touches a dead person, any human being who has died, shall be unclean for seven days.
That person shall be purified on the third day and on the seventh day, and he shall be clean. If he is not purified on the third day and on the seventh day, he shall not be clean.

Whosoever touches the dead body of any human being who has died, and is not purified, has defiled the Tent of the Lord; that soul shall be wiped out from Israel. Because water of sprinkling was not sprinkled upon him, he is unclean; his uncleanness is still in him.
And whatever the unclean person touches shall be unclean, and the person who touches it shall be unclean until evening.

Haggai answered, “So is this people, and so is this nation before Me, says the Lord; so are all the works of their hands, and whoever approaches there will be defiled because of their morning gains. They will suffer because of their labors, and you hated those who rebuked at the gates.
They hated one who reproved at the gates and abhorred a holy word.
And now, please set your hearts on the time before this day, before stone was placed upon stone in the sanctuary of the Lord,
on how things were with you: when you put twenty sata of barley into a bin, there were ten sata of barley; when you went to the wine vat to draw fifty metretai, there were twenty.

You sowed much and brought in little; you ate, but were not satisfied; you drank, but not to intoxication; you clothed yourselves, but were not warmed in them. The one gathering wages gathered them into a bundle with holes.
I struck you with barrenness, damage from wind and hail—all the works of your hands—and you did not turn to Me, says the Lord.
“I struck you with burning and jaundice. You multiplied your gardens; the caterpillar devoured your vineyards, fig orchards and olive groves, yet not even so did you turn to Me,” says the Lord.

Thus says the Lord Almighty: Let your hands be strong, you who hear these words in these days from the prophets’ mouth, from the day when the house of the Lord Almighty was founded, and from when the temple was built.
whether it will yet be recognized on the threshing floor, and whether the vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate and the olive trees still bear no fruit. From this day I will bless.”
Now I do not act toward this people’s remnant as in the former days, says the Lord Almighty,
but I will show peace: the vine will give its fruit, the earth its produce, and heaven its dew. I will give My people’s remnant all these as an inheritance.
As you were under a curse among the nations, house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will preserve you, and you will be in blessing. Take courage and be strong in your hands.

I will summon every fear against him, says the Lord. A man’s sword will be against his brother.

triples.relationship: later citation of the promise to shake heaven and earth once more
triples.rationale: Haggai promises once more to shake heaven and earth, sea and dry land; Hebrews quotes the promise to shake earth and heaven once more and reflects on the removal of shaken things. The explicit repeated wording establishes the citation relationship.

triples.relationship: nations' valuable offerings and the glorification of God's house
triples.rationale: Haggai says the nations' choice things will come and His house will be filled with glory; Isaiah describes nations' wealth, gold and offerings arriving, followed by the glorification of God's house. The relationship follows the native plural choice things rather than substituting a singular personal title.

triples.relationship: all temple resources belong to God
triples.rationale: Haggai declares silver and gold His; David acknowledges that everything given for God's house comes from God's own hand and belongs to Him. The surrounding temple donations include gold and silver, making the ownership statement materially specific.

triples.relationship: divine gift of peace extending to inner life
triples.rationale: Haggai promises peace in the place and peace of soul for those building the sanctuary; Jesus gives His peace and tells the disciples not to have troubled or afraid hearts. The thematic parallel concerns inward peace as a divine gift, not identification of the builders with the disciples.

triples.rationale: The oracle is dated to the twenty-fourth of the ninth month; the later instruction repeats that date as the day from which the people should direct their hearts. The repeated date connects the current message with its stated turning point.

The shared rebuke concerns unheeded discipline, not identical agents of crop damage.

The shared signet image is used for selection in one and removal in the other, without resolving all dynastic implications.
